solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resuscitate space-traveller with oxygen

definitions.note: the answer is intransitive (to revive), the clue word transitive; the sense of reviving carries it

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An astronaut is revived with an oxygen supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, which is what resuscitation brings about.

clue.text: Price a wealthy husband exchanged for a place in Central America

indicators.note: one thing exchanged for another is swapped out and replaced

parts.note: H abbreviates husband; this letter is swapped out

explanation.surface: Someone weighs the cost of trading a rich spouse for a home in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: RICH loses its H in favour of A, giving RICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a country lying between Nicaragua and Panama on the Central American isthmus.

clue.text: In old college, butter up physicist

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A scientist at his former college is flattered by the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter up looks like a phrase meaning flatter; split it, and a butter is one that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian physicist and pioneer of radio transmission.

clue.text: Gallery concealing overdraft until now

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it within

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft

explanation.surface: An art gallery has been hiding its debts up to the present.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, with its best-known branches in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is an idiom meaning up to the present time.

clue.text: Gets rid of watches elsewhere

parts.note: a fob is a pocket watch on a chain

explanation.surface: Someone disposes of timepieces somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: To fob someone or something off is to dismiss or offload it with an excuse.

clue.text: Story following a conservative after leaving university

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is removed

parts.note: F abbreviates following, as in page references
blue is the colour of the Conservative Party
U abbreviates university; it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A tale about trailing a Tory once he has left university.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with talking animals, that teaches a moral.

clue.text: Unmissable target on board, right? Wrong!

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A darts player is told a dead certain shot on the board is a miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, someone who could not hit a barn door is a very poor shot, so it is a target too big to miss.

clue.text: Paper folding over capital mistake lacking investment

indicators.note: a word lacking something has had that part taken out

parts.note: O abbreviates over, a cricket term
Riga is the capital of Latvia
a stake is an investment; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Paper creased over a costly error made without funding.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Fast ships leave on time

definitions.note: two senses at once: fast as an adjective and a group of ships

parts.note: to flee is to leave quickly

explanation.surface: Speedy vessels depart punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works twice: fleet as an adjective means swift, and as a noun a navy's ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means nimble and swift, and also a body of vessels sailing together.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker's complaint, swallowing a drop

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside

parts.note: gout is an ailment, a complaint
a dab is a small drop or spot

explanation.surface: A hedonist's gout comes from downing one more glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint reads as a grumble, but in crosswords it often means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout roams from one social event to the next in search of fun.

clue.text: Scrap rake-head in shack

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut or shack

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rake's head is thrown away in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment of something.

clue.text: Inn stocking popular fruit

indicators.note: a shop stocking an item holds it within

parts.note: auberge is the French word for an inn, used in English too

explanation.surface: A pub keeps a well-liked fruit on its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruit looks wrong for a vegetable, but botanically the aubergine is a berry; Americans call it eggplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine is botanically a berry, so calling it produce of the fruit kind is fair.

clue.text: Sailor abroad fathoms expert reversal

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fathom

explanation.surface: A seafarer overseas makes a skilled change of course in deep water.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete turnaround in direction or opinion.

clue.text: Doled out diamonds, playing late

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely into another order

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player hands out diamonds while playing late into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are dealt, that is distributed, so dealt means handed out in shares.

clue.text: Murdoch's uneven coverage of air-raids

indicators.note: patchy coverage takes only every other letter, skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A media mogul's newspapers report wartime bombing patchily.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the press baron Rupert; it is the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist and philosopher, so her surname stands for her forename.

clue.text: Gofers of interest to the canine anatomist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: menial helpers who run errands and do the drudge work

definitions.text: of interest to the canine anatomist?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read playfully: the bodies of dogs, which a vet studying dog anatomy would examine

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: split the word as dogs' bodies. A dogsbody is British slang for a drudge who gets the jobs nobody else wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a lowly worker given the tedious errands, exactly what a gofer runs.

clue.text: More careless birdwatcher breaking silence rule

indicators.note: something breaking into a sequence goes in the middle of it

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
Bill Oddie is a British TV birdwatcher and comedian

explanation.surface: A twitcher carelessly breaks the rule of silence in the hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Oddie is a well-known British TV birdwatcher; the silence and the rule are two separate pieces that he splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means badly done, so shoddier work is sloppier or more careless.

clue.text: Small, tense eejit landing after a flight

parts.note: an eejit is an Irish idiot, and an airhead is a fool

explanation.surface: A small, nervous fool touches down after a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Landing after a flight suggests an aircraft; it is the top of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairhead is the landing at the top of a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Irish statesman read out farewell therein

indicators.note: therein means inside that, so one piece goes within the other
letters out of place have been put into a new order

parts.note: vale is the Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A goodbye message for an Irish politician is read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Vale is Latin, familiar from valedictory speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamon de Valera was Ireland's Taoiseach and later its President.

clue.text: Refusal to vote for obstinate new leader's motion

indicators.note: letters in motion are moved around into a new order
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone declines to back a stubborn incoming leader's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion looks like the thing being voted on, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstention is a deliberate decision not to cast a vote either way.

clue.text: Muck-raking Manxman maybe losing his head

definitions.note: a verb form defining a noun; the sense of smearing carries it

indicators.note: losing one's head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so he is one example

explanation.surface: A man from the Isle of Man digs up scandal and is beheaded for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation, the spreading of damaging gossip that muck-raking involves.

clue.text: Parks in Truro, say

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their join

parts.note: the end of Truro running into the start of say

explanation.surface: Someone describes the public gardens of a Cornish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Parks looks like green spaces; it is the civil-rights figure. Truro is the county town of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosa Parks was the American civil-rights activist, so her surname points to her first name.

clue.text: Prepared to carve ham

indicators.note: ingredients that are prepared are reworked, as these letters are

explanation.surface: A cook is ready to slice the ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham looks like the meat being carved; it is a verb for bad acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, which is overacting.

clue.text: Might he be seen out on the tiles?

definitions.text: Might he be seen out on the tiles?

parts.note: surface reading: someone out partying all night

parts.words: Might he be seen out on the tiles?
parts.note: setter's reading: a tradesman literally working up on a roof

explanation.walkthrough: Out on the tiles is a British idiom for a night of revelry; here the tiles are roofing.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater is a roofer who lays slate tiles, so he works on the tiles.

clue.text: Have a drink before a play

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A theatregoer has a quick drink before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, screen or radio.

clue.text: Doctor a newspaper sketch

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with a newspaper cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a verb meaning falsify; it is just the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, as a sketch is.

clue.text: Where to find hammer in Tolkien's world after principal characters in The Hobbit have vanished

indicators.note: what has vanished is no longer present, so it is taken away

parts.note: Tolkien set his fantasy books in this land

indicators.note: the principal characters are the leading letters of each word

parts.note: the first letters of the two title words, removed from the end

explanation.surface: Fantasy fans hunt for a weapon in Tolkien's world once the main Hobbit characters are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Principal characters suggests Bilbo and company; it means the opening letters. The hammer is not a tool but a tiny bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer, or malleus, is one of the three small bones in the middle ear.

clue.text: Major eastern state

explanation.surface: An important state on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA.

clue.text: Confused, reading extremely dense French novelist

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A reader is baffled by a very difficult French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French author who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1947.

clue.text: Josh drinks ale at the close

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A man named Josh sips beer at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh reads as a name, but it is the verb to rib, and drinks looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh is to tease someone in a good-humoured way.

clue.text: Sailor volunteers starters of river eel served raw

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: the starters of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of river and eel

explanation.surface: A seaman and helpers dish up uncooked eel from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters looks like a menu course, which suits the food surface, but it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare or tuna tartare is a dish of finely chopped raw meat or fish.

clue.text: Old republican at English department lectured

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A veteran Republican gave a talk at an English faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, so orated means gave a lecture.
